title: Light in the bass drum and never retuning heads
summary: He keeps a light in the bass drum to keep the head dry and tight, and never broke a head on a drum he had for years.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Yeah, a lot of them. I'd like to ask you something about your drums, Alec. I noticed you have it rigged up for a light in the bass drum. Yeah. You keep a light in that? Oh, yeah. Do you do that just for effect or is there any reason for that?

Well, I'll tell you the reason why I keep a light, life is damp. Or if I'm playing in a place where they got a lot of people that keep my drums this tight. You see, in other words, the man that I have to take a lesson from, if I tell you all something, probably you all may not believe me. I had that drum about 18 or 19 years.
And I ain't never broke a head. I've heard of people that right there.
And Lady Bailey says that he never broke a drum head. Huh? Lady Bailey says he never broke a drum head.
Well, I'll tell you, I ain't never broke a drum head. I said those are the same.
And I ain't never broke down on that.

And I won't show you. And I had never said before that I hadn't broke down on that. But the man I have to take a lesson from, I said Cantrell, he told me don't never take and tighten the drum head and untighten.
If you tighten it to a certain tune, let it stay like that.
Let it stay like that. I don't tighten my snare drum.
I don't tighten my bass drum. If I finally got my tune that I like, I put my light on. Them globes I got, they'll bring it up. What have you got in there?
